notes.title: A new price and a new update on their way
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

Big news today: starting December 19th, Spiral will see its price cut permanently to 19.99$, right on time for the Winter Sale!

When we reflected on what Spiral's price should be, given the work that went into it and what we offered, we chose a price that we felt (and we still feel) was fair. However, our goal is also to have Spiral shared with as many people as possible, and we don't want the price to be an obstacle to people who wish to experience it.

So, if there is someone you know who is still on the fence, don't hesitate to let them know! The holiday is coming; Spiral would feel really at home in that cozy sock full of love and goodies you're giving to your loved one. 

We're also working on a new patch at the moment, so keep your eyes peeled.

Thank you so much for being there; we love you and are really grateful for you. Take care and talk soon.

notes.title: Spiral’s Release Day is Here!
notes.notes:
Hello folks,

Today is an incredibly exciting and emotional day for everyone here at Folklore Games -- our very first game, Spiral, has officially released here on Steam! 🎉🎉🎉

Grab it now! https://store.steampowered.com/app/1579390/Spiral/ 

To celebrate the launch, we will be offering the bundle, including Spiral’s art book and soundtrack, for the price of the base game during the first week!

After over four years in development, many talented people coming together and perseverance, we are excited to present you Bernard’s story. This project has been a personal one for us to create, and we’ve seen through events that we’ve been to, to our lovely players on Discord and socials that it’s been an equally emotional one for some of you! We only hope that Spiral will be able to create more awareness, discussion and empathy for people like Bernard - but also remind you to celebrate those cherished memories with your own loved ones.

If you’ve had a chance to play the game and want to help our team, please consider leaving a review on Steam. Reviews help indies like us immensely when it comes to breaking through the noise here on Steam and each and every one makes a difference! If you’re thinking of leaving one, we thank you from the bottom of our hearts! 💖

We cannot thank you enough for being on this journey with us, and we hope your time with Bernard is a positive one! Your support throughout this journey has meant the world and we are so happy to finally share this story with you all. 💜

PS. If you ever wanna chat, don’t be afraid to say hi!

notes.title: Recap of 2023 and Happy Holidays!
notes.notes:
With 2023 coming to an end, we felt it was the perfect time to make a recap of the last year and everything that happened during those oh-so-brief twelve months. So sit down tight, and let's start!


[h2]Winter[/h2]
When the year started, we had five scenes that still needed some polish but were mostly finished, three that had their initial layout, and two for which most of the structure was already there. Our script was complete (aside from two scenes that had been put on hold), and we were preparing for an overhaul of the subtitles system.

With that, we were ready to push the game even further during the year, and our first event came in fast when we were picked to take part of the Demo Nights in January! In early March, to celebrate the release anniversary of Spiral's demo, we updated it with the new subtitle system as well as the addition of both Italian and Turkish localization!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40281236/f7b28c8ab532a87170f400311f79efcd1b013c0d.png[/img]


[h2]Spring[/h2]
Spring started with a roar for us. We had two enormous events happening at the same time! We went to PAX East to present Spiral for the very first time, and while we were there, we had to handle our Kickstarter campaign! Each of these would have already put some pressure on us, but both of them, at the same time, were a lot for our little team! But no matter what, we pushed through!

We were able to meet so many of you at PAX East, and as always, it was a blast to see you enjoy Spiral and all the effort we've put into it. Talking with you all warms our hearts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40281236/4ce65844c9b2ecf8d51ed582346767781a55c44c.png[/img]

Our Kickstarter campaign was another opportunity to connect with so many new people. We had new people reaching out to us or joining our community each day. All the love we received from you still pushes us forward to this day. Just in case we didn't say it enough, thank you!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40281236/e693372e967e98f6844ade0c3269fce3665c9796.jpg[/img]

And let's not forget that during this time, we had finally officially announced we would be releasing on PS5, Xbox and Switch!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40281236/31b0915d546c45d3187f4c7e17befdf451e38e02.png[/img]


[h2]Summer[/h2]
The summer was more peaceful after such an intense spring, but we still have some highlights.

It's when we announced our partnership with SpaceJazz! They would help us bring Spiral to China and take care of localizing the game in Chinese, allowing it to reach even more people.

We were also able to attend the Montreal Comiccon once more, and by now, you know how much we enjoy meeting you and seeing you react to Spiral's demo whenever we can :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40281236/f0ac499a3958d688c3d701cc32fcb84715c9ee5a.png[/img]


[h2]Fall[/h2]
When fall arrived, we were waiting for it with a strong announcement, and for it, we were able to be part of The MIX showcase during PAX West. While the team was unfortunately unable to have a booth there this year, Spiral was still present through their showcase to announce the big news.

[b]Spiral will be released in September 2024![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40281236/75559d82c5a16ac631b0c1b89066e3044352c57e.jpg[/img]

To make it even more memorable, we released an updated trailer with scenes never shown before and an all-new key art that would represent Spiral everywhere from now on!



And now, the year is coming to an end. There's still so much left to share with you next year, and we can't wait to finally put Spiral in your hands. As far as how much progress we made, rather than giving vague states of some scenes, let me put everything in perspective. The final game will contain a total of 20 scenes (memories). Of those:
	
[list]
[*] Only 3 haven't been worked on in the engine
[*] 14 out of 20 have been visually dressed
[*] 15 out of 20 are playable from start to finish (even if some are still quite buggy ^^)
[/list]


There's still a lot of work to do, but the end is in sight, and we're psych about it!

We wish you all happy holidays and hope you can spend all the time you want tucked away with your loved ones.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40281236/45e5e5ca03896151a4e4c004fbda119cf15696dd.jpg[/img]

The Folklore Games team

notes.title: Format Update
notes.notes:
Hello Everyone!

First off, for those that don't want to read through all the details, here's the essential: Spiral will release as a single experience; it won't be episodic anymore.

I'll go next with probably the interrogation most of you now have: no, it won't change our planned 2023 release date! We're not immune to delays, but we're also a cunning bunch. When we first created the page, we decided to go with the worst of both worlds, assuming it was best to give a pleasant surprise rather than a bad one! If we had decided to commit to the episodic format, the actual first episode would have been released this year, not in 2023 ^^

Now, as for why we decided to drop the episodic format? Well, since the very beginning, we wanted Spiral to be a single experience. However, since we're self-funded, we were aware that it would take a lot of time and investment, and eventually, we decided to open the door to the idea of releasing it episodically to help fund subsequent episodes. Not to make sure they would be created, that was always a certainty for us, but rather to accelerate development and bring Spiral to life earlier.

It came, of course, with the caveats that a lot of people aren't fans of the episodic format, especially publishers! Our goal was, is and always will be to do what's best for the game and its development. This is precisely why we're dropping the episodic format for good. In the past few months, we realized that while the first scenes of the game were nearly complete, so many things could still influence or improve them while we worked on the rest of the game, and releasing them now on their own would prevent them from being as great as they would be in a full release. And in addition to that, we've already been able to pick up the development pace, and things are looking good.

That's all for today, but if you have any questions, feel free to reach out!

Take care
